title: PromiseCreated.v1
description: Payload of the PromiseCreated event (A§23). Emitted by arrangement-service — the single producer (A§7.2) — when a promise to pay is captured via `POST /v1/promises` (by a collector in the workbench or by treatment execution). A promise is a customer *commitment* to pay one amount by one date; an arrangement is the structured multi-instalment plan — they are distinct aggregates with distinct state machines (D§10, A§10.2 PROPOSED -> ACCEPTED -> KEPT|BROKEN|CANCELLED). Published on `collections.arrangement` keyed by `promiseId`, not by the channel context, so both promise events for one promise stay ordered (A§23/§26). Rides the A§24 envelope; a breaking change ships as PromiseCreated.v2 (D§29).

promiseId.description: Platform identifier of the promise. Equal to the envelope `aggregateId` and the Kafka partition key of this event (A§23 names `promiseId` as the key for promise events, even though they share the `collections.arrangement` topic with arrangement events).

caseId.description: Platform identifier of the case the promise was made on. A promise is always taken in the context of a case (it is the output of a collections conversation), so this is required and never null.

accountId.description: Platform identifier of the account the promised money is for, so payment-service and analytics can join on the account without calling the arrangement API.

amountMinor.description: Amount the customer promised to pay, in minor units of `currency`. Strictly positive: a promise of zero is not a promise.

currency.description: ISO-4217 alpha-3 currency of `amountMinor`; always the account's currency.

dueDate.description: Calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD) by which the promised amount is due. The breach tick compares this against its `--as-of` date to decide whether the promise is broken (SVC-5), which is why it is a business date and not a timestamp.
